subject.title: transcripts: show prints stored terminal escapes from imported text

question: Should transcript escape sanitization happen when summaries are persisted, only when `transcripts show` writes to a terminal, or at both boundaries?
rationale: Sanitizing at persistence changes stored `summary.md` and `summary.json` semantics, while display-only sanitization leaves dangerous bytes in local artifacts; that storage/display boundary needs maintainer security intent.

options.title: Sanitize summary inputs before persistence
options.body: Strip terminal escapes from imported utterance text and speaker labels before summary JSON/markdown are written, so stored summary artifacts are safe by default.

options.title: Sanitize only terminal display
options.body: Leave stored artifacts byte-preserving but strip controls in non-JSON `transcripts show` output, preserving raw summaries at the cost of unsafe local files.

options.title: Sanitize both persistence and display
options.body: Defend both stored artifacts and stdout, but document the intentionally non-byte-preserving summary behavior.

recommendation.title: Sanitize summary inputs before persistence
recommendation.body: Strip terminal escapes from imported utterance text and speaker labels before summary JSON/markdown are written, so stored summary artifacts are safe by default.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle owns the strongest current implementation and merge-history signal for the transcript CLI and summary surface.
